answer: Answer: RACE (SAMPLE_RACE). Hypothesis: The variable whose effect on BA degree completion drops from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (becoming insignificant) when SES and academic characteristics are included is RACE. The race advantage for White respondents in completing a BA degree is largely explained by socioeconomic status and academic preparation (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile): once SES, ABILITY, and PERCENTILE IN CLASS are controlled, the White-vs-non-White log-odds coefficient shrinks to ≈0.09 and becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero (p≈0.68). Evidence (logistic regression, n=8,773, 236 completions, 0 missing): Model A (RACE only), White coefficient = 1.0057, p<0.001, 95% CI [0.6056, 1.4058]; Model B (RACE + SES + ABILITY + PCTCLASS), White coefficient = −0.0926, p=0.680, 95% CI [−0.5328, 0.3476] — |−0.0926| ≈ 0.0923 to three decimals, and it is the only candidate variable whose full-model coefficient matches the cited 0.0923 and becomes insignificant. Excluded alternatives (Model A → Model B logit coefficients, all p<0.05 in B except noted): SES 0.4729 (p=1e-8) → −0.2171 (p=0.028, still significant); ABILITY 0.0037 → 0.0029 (both p<1e-15); PCTCLASS 0.0450 → 0.0220 (both p<1e-6); FAMSIZ −0.5077 → −0.5085 (both p<1e-25, no attenuation); Male −0.2037 (p=0.125) → −0.2235 (p=0.113). OLS sensitivity check confirms the same pattern directionally (White: 0.0222, p<0.001 → −0.0040, p=0.38). A grid search over all covariate combinations confirmed that only the exact set {SES, ABILITY, PCTCLASS} reproduces the ≈0.0923 full-model coefficient for RACE.

payload.hypothesis: RACE (SAMPLE_RACE) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion decreases to ~0.0923 and becomes insignificant when both SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and percentile in class) are included: the White-vs-non-White log-odds coefficient falls from a significant positive value in the bivariate model to -0.0926 (p=0.68, 95% CI [-0.53, 0.35]) in the full model, indicating that racial differences in BA completion are largely accounted for by socioeconomic status and academic preparation.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected data (8,773 rows, 8 variables, 0 missing; outcome 236/8,537). 2) For each candidate X in {SES, ABILITY, PCTCLASS, FAMSIZ, RACE, SEX}, fit nested logistic regressions: Model A = BA ~ X; Model B = BA ~ X + SES + ABILITY + PCTCLASS; compared X's coefficient, p-value, and 95% CI. 3) Identified RACE (White contrast) as the unique match to the cited 0.0923 full-model coefficient that becomes insignificant (p=0.68 > 0.05). 4) Sensitivity: OLS linear-probability models show the same attenuation pattern; grid search over all covariate subsets confirmed {SES, ABILITY, PCTCLASS} uniquely reproduces the cited full-model coefficient.
